help.volume: Track volume, as a % of the instrument’s: 0% is silent, 100% unchanged.
help.pan: Pan, in %: + to the right, − to the left, 0 in the center. At +100% the sound comes out of the right only; at −100%, out of the left only.
help.lowPass: Low-pass cutoff, in hertz: highs above it are attenuated. At 20,000 Hz, everything passes.
help.highPass: High-pass cutoff, in hertz: lows below it are attenuated. At 20 Hz, everything passes.
help.resonance: Filter resonance, in %: boosts the frequencies near the low-pass and high-pass cutoffs. 0%: none.
help.reverb: Share of reverberated sound, in %: 0% is dry, no reverb.
help.detune: Unison detune, in cents (hundredths of a semitone): the spread between its voices. Only heard with 2 voices or more.

source.label: Sound source

source.fileTitle: Analysis of a WAV, FLAC or MP3 file

mic.title: Microphone
mic.nothingRecorded: Nothing is recorded: only the note and the partials are shown.
mic.idle: synthway-core opens the microphone when you click Listen or Record, and closes it when you stop or leave the tab.
mic.exclusive: Exclusive mode: the sound arrives without Windows audio effects (noise reduction, automatic gain). While listening, other applications can’t use this microphone.
mic.shared: Shared mode: Windows refused exclusive mode, so its audio effects apply. Noise reduction can smother a held note. Turn off the microphone’s “Audio enhancements” in Windows Settings (System › Sound).
mic.connectionLost: Connection to the server lost: the microphone is closed.

record.title: Recording
record.playTitle: Play the recording from the cursor, which follows it (stops listening). Space: play / pause
record.startTitle: Record what the microphone hears, with no time limit
record.inProgress: Recording… {seconds} s. Stop whenever you like.
record.hint: Click “Record”: the microphone opens and everything it hears is kept, with no time limit.
record.placeholder: The recording’s waveform will show here. Nothing is played.
record.noCursor: click the recording to analyze a moment, drag to select a zone to loop, or click “Play”: listening stops.
record.withCursor: a click picks the moment analyzed and where “Play” starts (arrows: ±10 ms), a drag selects a zone to loop. “Listen” goes back to live and removes the cursor.
record.lost: {seconds} s lost during recording (the server couldn’t keep up), replaced by silence.

file.title: File
file.playTitle: Play the file from the cursor, which follows it. Space: play / pause
file.clearestTitle: Move the cursor to the moment where the note is clearest
file.drop: Drop a WAV, FLAC or MP3 file here, or click “Import a sound”.
file.dropNote: A held note gives the clearest reading. Nothing is played.
file.info: {duration} · {rate} kHz · the pink dots follow the note along the file. A click picks the moment analyzed and where “Play” starts (arrows: ±10 ms), a drag selects a zone to loop.

note.title: Note
note.autoTitle: The note heard (on a zone, the lowest of its clear notes)
note.fixedTitle: Ratios are taken to the chosen note, in its octave
note.autoNote: Ratios are taken to the note heard. On a zone, it is the lowest of its clear notes: a fundamental that fades before its harmonics doesn’t make it jump an octave. Fix it if you know the note played.
note.fixedNote: Ratios are taken to {note}, tuned to what the Analyzer hears of that note in any octave. Moments on another note don’t count. Doesn’t apply to live listening.

spectrum.title: Spectrum
spectrum.gateOn: Peaks under the yellow line are ignored: they are no longer partials, and with no partial above it, there is no note.
spectrum.gateHint: Raise it just above the background noise (fan, hiss) so the analysis ignores it.
spectrum.windowLive: For the cursor and zones. Live, from the microphone, the analysis keeps its usual window (about 170 ms).
spectrum.windowZone: With a zone, the analysis runs windows of this length across the whole zone (up to 100, at least 10 ms apart) and keeps the median of each partial.
spectrum.windowMoment: The cursor analyzes this length around it (the green bounds on the waveform). Shorter: more precise in time; longer: finer in frequency, and better for low notes.
spectrum.windowTooShort: {note} ({frequency} Hz) needs at least {min} ms to separate its harmonics: at {window} ms, they blend together.
spectrum.windowTooLow: {note} is too low to separate its harmonics, even at {max} ms.

spectrumChart.label: Measured spectrum, in decibels by frequency
spectrumChart.empty: The spectrum shows as soon as a sound is analyzed

partials.title: Partials
partials.needNote: Needs a note and its partials: place the cursor or select a zone on a sound
partials.makeZone: Build a trial instrument from these partials and each one’s envelope, measured on the zone, played on the keyboard below. Nothing is saved.
partials.makeMoment: Build a trial instrument from these partials (ratios and amplitudes), played on the keyboard below. Nothing is saved.
partials.remakeZone: Rebuild the trial instrument from these partials and each one’s envelope, measured on the zone, played on the keyboard below. Nothing is saved.
partials.remakeMoment: Rebuild the trial instrument from these partials (ratios and amplitudes), played on the keyboard below. Nothing is saved.
partials.empty: Place the cursor or select a zone on a sound.
partials.harmonicsOnlyHint: Within {cents} cents of a whole ratio: leaves out the other instruments of a mix (not live)
partials.envelopeZone: The trial instrument also gets each partial’s envelope, measured on the zone: make the zone run from the note’s attack to the next note.
partials.envelopeMoment: With a zone on a single note, from its attack to the next note, the trial instrument also gets each partial’s envelope.
partials.noPeak: No peak stands out from the noise.
partials.placeholder: The partials of the analyzed sound show here, from lowest to highest.

zoneNotes.single: A single note, over its time in the zone: ratios are taken to it, the other notes are left out (their shared harmonics stay mixed in).
zoneNotes.several: Several notes played together or one after another: the zone analysis takes them as one. Pick one for its own timbre, or keep the whole zone for an instrument that plays the whole chord on a single key.
zoneNotes.severalNamed: Several notes played together or one after another: the zone analysis takes them as one, {note}. Pick one for its own timbre, or keep the whole zone for an instrument that plays the whole chord on a single key.
zoneNotes.heard: Notes heard in the zone: click one to analyze it alone.
zoneNotes.chipTitle: Analyze {name} alone, from {start} to {end} s: ratios taken to {name} ({frequency} Hz). Strength {strength}% of the strongest.
zoneNotes.wholeZoneTitle: Go back to the selected zone and the automatic reference note
zoneNotes.others: The zone holds notes other than {note} ({percent}% of the time). They are left out, but a zone on a single note, from its attack to the next one, gives the clearest result.

build.envelopesEmpty: The envelope measurement found no note and no partial in this zone.
build.neverAlone: This note is never heard alone here: pick a note from the chips, or “Measured partials”.
build.noShape: No waveform measured here: choose “Measured partials”.
build.envelopeSingle: a single envelope (a zone on a single note gives each partial its own)
build.shape_one: Shape {shape} ({gap} dB deviation): {count} harmonic as a sine wave, {filter}, {envelope}.
build.shape_other: Shape {shape} ({gap} dB deviation): {count} harmonics as sine waves, {filter}, {envelope}.
build.shapeEnvelopeZone: the envelope measured on its strongest partial for all of them
build.description: Made in the Analyzer from {origin}: {analyzed}, ratios to {note}{harmonics}. {made}

trial.stale: The selection or settings have changed since: the instrument stays as it is, “Update” rebuilds it with them.
trial.live: Made from what the microphone heard at the click: “Update” takes what it hears now.
trial.compareNote: Play {note} (the green dot) and compare with the original. Nothing is kept until you click “Save”.
trial.compare: Play it and compare with the original. Nothing is kept until you click “Save”.
trial.backTitle: Restore the zone (or moment) and the reference note the trial instrument came from
trial.updateTitle: Rebuild the trial instrument from the selection and settings shown
trial.playOriginalTitle: Loop the selected zone, to compare
trial.playOriginalNoZone: Select a zone on the sound to hear it again in a loop
trial.discardTitle: Close the trial without keeping anything
trial.saveTitle: Add the instrument to the library and open it in the Instrument Creator
trial.markedNote: {note}: the analyzed note, which should sound like the original

waveFit.title: Waveform
waveFit.buildFromTitle: What “Try instrument” builds the instrument from: the measured partials, or the harmonics of a waveform, with its low-pass
waveFit.empty: Place the cursor or select a zone on a sound: the waveform of its note shows here.
waveFit.neverAlone: {note} is never heard alone here: probably a chord over its missing fundamental. Pick a note from the chips to get the waveform of each one.
waveFit.weakNote: The measured note, {note}, is weak in the zone ({percent}% of the strongest). Pick a note from the chips.
waveFit.weakNoteStrong: The measured note, {note}, is weak in the zone ({percent}% of the strongest): the strong notes are {notes}. Pick one of them from the chips.
waveFit.fitTitle: {shape}: {hint}. Average deviation of {gap} dB from the measured harmonics. Click to build the trial from it.
waveFit.fitTitleLowpass: {shape}: {hint}. Average deviation of {gap} dB from the measured harmonics, through this low-pass. Click to build the trial from it.
waveFit.evenPresent: present ({db} dB vs. the neighboring odd ones)
waveFit.evenWeakened: weakened ({db} dB vs. the neighboring odd ones)
waveFit.evenAbsent: absent ({db} dB vs. the neighboring odd ones)
waveFit.legend: Bars: the measured harmonics (gray: shared with another note, left out; faint: not above the noise floor). Dots: {shape}. The deviation is the average gap, in dB, between the two; phase can’t be heard on a held note and isn’t measured.
waveFit.poor: No shape really fits (the closest is {gap} dB off): the measured partials stay more faithful.
waveFit.fair: Close: compare by ear with the measured partials.
waveFit.chartLabel: Level of each measured harmonic, and that of the chosen shape
waveFit.barShared: , shared with another note: left out

warnings.limit: Engine limit reached: at most {max} partials per instrument.
warnings.aliasing: Above half the sample rate ({nyquist}), a partial folds back as another frequency: {list}.
warnings.aliasingMore_one: Above half the sample rate ({nyquist}), a partial folds back as another frequency: {list}, and {count} more (marked in the partial list).
warnings.aliasingMore_other: Above half the sample rate ({nyquist}), a partial folds back as another frequency: {list}, and {count} more (marked in the partial list).
warnings.peak: Possible clipping: the sum of the amplitudes × the volume reaches {peak}. If the partials peak together, the sound goes over 100% and will be clipped.
warnings.reverb: Possible clipping with the reverb: it can push the peaks toward {peak}. Lower the volume if the sound clips.
warnings.unison: Possible clipping with unison: when its {voices} voices line up in phase, the peaks can rise toward {peak}. Lower the volume if the sound clips.

reverb.title: Reverb
reverb.hint: A room of about 2 s that keeps ringing after the note. At 100%, only the reverb remains.

unison.title: Unison
unison.hint: Each partial is played by several slightly detuned oscillators that beat against each other: the sound thickens, like a “supersaw”. 5 to 7 voices at ±10–20 cents give the classic thickness; the width spreads them between left and right.

presets.hologramSine: A pure, crystal-clear sine, without a single extra harmonic.
presets.rainCityBass: A deep, dark square to lay down the groove.
presets.sirenFx: A piercing square for alarms and effects.
presets.hazePad: A slow triangle pad, like a neon haze.
presets.chromePluck: Sharp attack and short decay, for arpeggios.
presets.neonLead: A cutting sawtooth, built for melodies.
presets.glassOrgan: Six sustained harmonics, like the drawbars of an organ.
presets.pluckedString: Eight harmonics at 1/n: the highest fade out first.
presets.neonBell: Inharmonic bell partials, each with its own length.
presets.shadowSupersaw: Measured on “Chasing Shadows” (other stem, 96.2 s): twelve softened sawtooth harmonics, 7 voices detuned by ±15 cents and spread in stereo, convex 90 ms attack. The song plays it as A5 + D6.
presets.shadowChord: The A5 + D6 chord of “Chasing Shadows” (other stem, 116.3 s) on a single key: play D4. Its two notes are harmonics 3 and 4 of D4, measured with their own. 5 voices at ±8 cents, convex 90 ms attack.
